newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1998 budget to go to next parliament.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1998 budget to go to next parliament.

text.p: The Polish government will present its 1998 budget draft in October to parliament chosen in the September 21 elections, the government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said on Tuesday.
"We decided to submit the budget in October and not by the end of September as earlier planned," Jakubowska told Reuters after a cabinet meeting.
"This is why it was not so pressing to discuss the budget draft on Tuesday. The government will discuss it at one of its coming sessions, before its summer holidays," she added.
The government goes on holidays in the second half of July. @

Finance Minister Marek Belka has said the 1998 budget draft will assume that inflation will fall to 9.5 percent next year from 14.6 percent in May and that the economy will continue to grow at 5.5 percent.

He has said the public debt, now at around 50 percent of gross domestic product, will be lowered by two points and budget deficit curbed to below two percent of GDP from 2.8 percent planned for this year.
